Plot per-peptide deltas from compare_states_tp(), by state pair and region

Source: R/plot_compare_states_tp.R
plot_compare_states_tp.Rd

compare_states_tp() itself has no plotting companion - unlike compare_states_unmatched() (paired with plot_compare_states_unmatched()) its peptide-by-pair result table was only ever inspected as a data.frame. This draws one panel per region (or a single "all" panel if regions wasn't used), with every matched peptide's delta shown as a box, violin, or plain jittered-point strip - one position per state pair - so a whole domain's behavior for a given comparison is visible at a glance, for any number of states.

Usage

plot_compare_states_tp(
  res,
  plot_type = c("jitter", "box", "violin"),
  sig_col = "firebrick",
  nonsig_col = "grey55",
  summary_col = "steelblue",
  tint = 0.6,
  point_cex = 0.9,
  jitter_width = 0.15,
  show_zero = TRUE,
  bg = "grey95",
  grid_col = "white",
  show_grid = TRUE,
  cex_annot = 0.9,
  font_family = ""
)

Arguments

res

the data.frame returned by compare_states_tp().

plot_type

one of "jitter" (every peptide as a point, no summary shape), "box", or "violin". Default "jitter".

sig_col

color for peptides with is_sig == TRUE. Default "firebrick".

nonsig_col

color for peptides with is_sig == FALSE. Default "grey55".

summary_col

color for the box/violin summary shape (drawn once per pair, pooling significant and non-significant peptides together). Default "steelblue".

tint

how much lighter than summary_col the box/violin fill is, 0 (no lightening) to 1 (white). Default 0.6.

point_cex

size of the jittered points. Default 0.9.

jitter_width

horizontal jitter width for points, as a fraction of pair spacing. Default 0.15.

show_zero

logical; draw a dashed horizontal reference line at delta = 0. Default TRUE.

bg

panel background color. Default "grey95"; use "white" for a plain white panel.

grid_col

gridline color drawn over bg. Default "white".

show_grid

logical; draw the shaded background/gridlines at all. Default TRUE.

cex_annot

text size for the "n significant / n tested" annotation under each region's title. Default 0.9.

font_family

font family passed to text-drawing calls. Default "" (device default).

Value

draws a one-panel-per-region base-R plot; returns NULL invisibly.

Showing every peptide, not only the significant ones

Every peptide tested is drawn, regardless of is_sig - significant ones are simply colored differently (sig_col vs nonsig_col) rather than filtered out. Looking only at a list of "significant peptides" hides exactly the pattern compare_states_unmatched()'s frac_peptides_significant diagnostic exists to catch: a region can contain a real, consistent shift in most of its peptides while still having only a few (or zero) individually clear the strict Hageman & Weis gate, or vice versa - one dramatic outlier peptide surrounded by otherwise flat ones. Seeing the whole distribution, not just the subset that cleared a cutoff, is the point of this plot.

On color and visibility

Box/violin fills are opaque colors (lightened by blending toward white in RGB space via tint, not by alpha transparency) deliberately - some graphics devices render semi-transparent fills as invisible or fully solid instead of blending them, so visibility here never depends on device compositing.

See also

compare_states_tp(), plot_compare_states_unmatched()

Examples

# \donttest{
file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
# the shipped example only has two states; compare_states_tp() needs 3+.
# See vignette("multistate") for a worked example with a synthetic third state.
# }
